newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian Metals - Singapore aluminium premiums jump.
newsitem.headline: Asian Metals - Singapore aluminium premiums jump.

text.p: Singapore aluminium premiums are surging due to tight supplies and strong regional demand for the metal, dealers said on Friday.
Premiums for western aluminium 20-25 kg ingots were quoted at US$70-$90 a tonne over London Metal Exchange (LME) cash prices against a quote of around $55-$75 about three weeks ago.
Indian and Russian aluminium ingots jumped to $55-$70 after hovering last month at around $40-$60, dealers said.
"Physical supplies of aluminium are really tight. There are a lot of people in this region looking for material," one said.
"Western aluminium ingots are very scarce in Singapore. That's why the premiums are rising," a Japanese dealer said.
One trader said his company had a customer looking for western aluminium ingots "and we couldn't get the material from the warehouse here. The premiums are now at least $90."
Traders said that aside from robust regional offtake, premiums have firmed partly because of falling aluminium stocks in the LME's Singapore warehouse.
LME aluminium investories here declined to 8,300 tonnes on Thursday, from 11,275 tonnes at the beginning of June.
The volume of shipments of aluminium from India's NALCO to Singapore have also dipped, one dealer said.
"The parcels they used to ship here would average 500-800 tonnes (a week). The parcels coming in now average only 300 tonnes," he said.
Aluminium premiums in regional markets such as Taiwan and Indonesia have climbed as a result, traders said.
Indonesian premiums were quoted at between $100-$110 a tonne CIF Jakarta while those in Taiwan were seen at $95-$100 CIF Kaoshiung and Keelung, they said.
"If it's prompt, it may even hit $110 in Taiwan," one said.
Indonesian buyers are trying to bargain the premiums down to $90, "but nobody will sell them material at $90. The minimum is $100," a dealer said.
In another development, Chinese zinc exporters are poised to jump into the market if LME zinc prices break through the psychological $1,400 barrier.
"The Chinese are just waiting for $1,400. Their selling orders are already in place," a dealer said.

Regional traders believe an estimated 5,000 to 10,000 tonnes of zinc remain off-warrant in Singapore and the Chinese are shipping an additional 5,000-10,000 tonnes of the metal to warehouses in the city-state over the next few weeks to take advantage of high prices.
"Somebody told me China has sent at least 5,000 tonnes of zinc to Singapore from Tianjin," a Japanese trader said.
The volume of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 26,500 tonnes on Thursday, up 1,250 tonnes from the previous day.
Three-month zinc was quoted by the trade at around $1,392/96 a tonne at 0340 GMT on Friday against the late quote on the LME on Thursday of $1,393/95 a tonne.
Zinc premiums in Singapore have softened to around $15-$30 from $25-$35 a few weeks ago.
"Zinc premiums are not going to move up due to the high prices on the LME," a dealer said.
"There's just too much zinc here," another trader said.

The copper market remained quiet in the region with the trade waiting for the arrival of around 20,000 tonnes of Chinese copper into warehouses in Singapore, dealers said. The shipment, however, is not expected to come in until mid-July.
-- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
